summary: Iran conducted multiple missile launches and UAV flights from Khuzestan province while jet activity was reported over Kermanshah and Shiraz. Israeli artillery and machine gun fire targeted multiple locations in southern Lebanon, accompanied by illumination bombs and warplanes over the Beqaa Valley. Israeli strikes in Gaza killed two senior Hamas internal security commanders, including the chief of the apparatus and the northern Gaza director.
key_points: Iran launched two missiles from Omidiyeh toward the south in Khuzestan province. (Source: @shin_persian/12897)
Iran launched a missile from Behbahan in Khuzestan province. (Source: @shin_persian/12900)
Iran launched a missile from Sarbandar in Khuzestan province. (Source: @shin_persian/12898)
Multiple UAV launches occurred from Omidiyeh and Behbahan in Khuzestan province. (Source: @shin_persian/12889,12899,12895)
Jet activity was heard over Kermanshah and Shiraz in Iran. (Source: @shin_persian/12893,12896)
Israeli artillery shelled Wadi al-Saluqi, Al-Mansouri, Zibqin, and Mazar'at Buyut al-Siyad in southern Lebanon. (Source: @redlinkleb/55129,55079,55068)
Israeli forces fired machine guns from Hula toward Talousa and dropped illumination bombs over Hula, Talousa, and between Shakra and Doubieh. (Source: @redlinkleb/55098,55066,55086)
Israeli strikes in Gaza killed Hamas internal security chief Naim Abu Nahal and northern Gaza director Muhammad Abu al-Awf with his family. (Source: @manniefabian/59584,59582)

points: Multiple missile launches detected from Khuzestan province: two missiles launched from Omidiyeh toward the south at 00:19 local time, one missile from Behbahan at 00:46 local time, and one missile from Sarbandar at 00:20 local time, all recorded via seismic/acoustic monitoring. (Source: @shin_persian/12897,12900,12898)

Repeated UAV launches from Omidiyeh at 1933Z and 00:42 local time, and at least three UAV launch sounds from Behbahan within a short period at 23:57 local time, indicating sustained unmanned aerial operations. (Source: @shin_persian/12889,12899,12895)

Two blasts heard in Sirik, Hormozgan province at 1929Z, assessed as possible missile launches; no blasts reported on Qeshm island. (Source: @shin_persian/12890)

sections.threat_assessment: Iran's simultaneous missile and UAV launches from multiple Khuzestan sites (Omidiyeh, Behbahan, Sarbandar) combined with jet activity over Kermanshah and Shiraz suggest a coordinated readiness exercise or potential response posture. Israeli strikes eliminating two top Hamas internal security leaders in Gaza City and Shati camp within 24 hours indicate a systematic decapitation campaign targeting the group's internal control apparatus. Sustained Israeli artillery, machine gun fire, and illumination bomb usage across southern Lebanon — from Wadi al-Saluqi to the Beqaa Valley — signals persistent pressure on Hezbollah border positions. The ISIS attack on Syrian Internal Security Forces in Al-Hasakah demonstrates the group's enduring capability to strike security infrastructure in northeast Syria. The unexplained projectile strike on a tanker 50 nautical miles west of Dubai raises concerns about maritime threats in the Gulf approaches.
sections.regional_response: Lebanese monitoring channels (RedAlertLebanon) document real-time Israeli artillery impacts, machine gun engagements, and illumination bomb deployments across the border sector, indicating active kinetic exchanges. Iranian missile/UAV launch activity is tracked by open-source acoustic sensors (FromIran) with 120-second delay, providing near-real-time strategic warning. Hamas publicly acknowledges the loss of its internal security chief and northern Gaza director, confirming Israeli targeting of the group's clandestine leadership. Syrian state media reports the Al-Hasakah ISIS attack details, including attacker fatalities, reflecting Damascus's narrative control. UKMTO's prompt maritime advisory on the Dubai tanker incident highlights international shipping awareness of Gulf security risks.
sections.intelligence_notes: The Khuzestan launch sites — Omidiyeh, Behbahan, Sarbandar — are known Iranian missile and UAV bases, suggesting the activity originates from established military infrastructure. Hamas's internal security apparatus, responsible for counterintelligence and asset protection, has now lost its top two leaders in rapid succession, potentially degrading the group's ability to safeguard hostages and sensitive information. Israeli use of illumination bombs over Hula, Talousa, and Shakra-Doubieh indicates nighttime tactical operations, likely to expose movement or guide fires. The Al-Hasakah ISIS attack targeted Internal Security Forces rather than SDF or coalition, possibly reflecting a shift toward softer regime-aligned targets. The tanker explosion near the Strait of Hormuz, attributed to an 'unidentified projectile,' warrants correlation with any Iranian naval or proxy activity in the Gulf of Oman.
